topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: Found my grandmother’s engagement ring, of all things, in a pawn shop. A glint of gold, a tiny diamond that always caught the light when she waved at the harvest moon. Those hands, so worn from the earth, so gentle when they rested on my head. The ring was cold in my fingers, not warm from the day’s toil, and it didn’t fit right. It shouldn’t be here, away from her stories and the smell of her herbs. I wonder what path brought it here, what harvests it witnessed before it slipped away. I should leave it, but I can’t. Not yet. The ring is a heavy weight, a reminder of days that faded like last year’s crop.
